simple.meaning: אַט (ʼaṭ) is a Hebrew word meaning “(as a noun) a necromancer (from their soft incantations), (as an adverb) gently.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: אַט (H328) appears 6 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Genesis 33:14, with occurrences in Genesis, 2 Samuel, 1 Kings, Job, Isaiah.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אַט (H328) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in אַט (H328) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: אַט (ʼaṭ) / H328 is traced through Genesis 33:14, 2 Samuel 18:5, 1 Kings 21:27, Job 15:11 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.short: (as a noun) a necromancer (from their soft incantations), (as an adverb) gently
definitions.full: H328. at אַט substantive gentleness, used only adverbially : — a. as adverb. accus . 1Kin 21:27 ַאט׃ וַיְהַלֵח and he (Ahab) went about softly (that is, in penitence); b. with לְ of norm or state (as in לָבֶטַח , see לְ ) 2Sam 18:5 לַנַּעַר לְאַטלִֿי (deal) gently for me with the young man, Isa 8:6 the waters of Shiloah לְאַ֑ט הַהֹלְכִים that go Gently ; with pretonic qameƒ Job 15:11 עִמָּֽח׃ לָאַט דָּבָר a word (spoken) gently with thee; with suffix Gen 33:14 and I לְאִטִּי אֶתְנַהֲלָה will lead on gently (literally according to my Gentleness ). לָאַט לְאַט gently , see אַט below אטט above לאך (√ of מְלָאכָה מַלְאָךְ , compare Arabic , send , messenger , Ethiopic send a messenger , see be sent, wait on, minister ; = Hebrew מַלְאָךְ ; compare Phoenician מלאך messenger ; Late Hebrew מַלְאָךְ Aramaic מַלְאֲכָא , as in Hebrew)
definitions.rootNote: from an unused root perhaps meaning to move softly;

occurrences.englishText: Please let my lord pass over before his servant, and I will lead on gently, according to the pace of the livestock that are before me and according to the pace of the children, until I come to my lord to Seir.”

The king commanded Joab and Abishai and Ittai, saying, “Deal gently for my sake with the young man, even with Absalom.” All the people heard when the king commanded all the captains concerning Absalom.
When Ahab heard those words, he tore his clothes, and put sackcloth on his flesh, and fasted, and lay in sackcloth, and went softly.
Are the consolations of God too small for you,
“Because this people has refused the waters of Shiloah that go softly, and rejoice in Rezin and Remaliah’s son;
The spirit of Egypt will fail within it. I will destroy its counsel. They will seek the idols, the charmers, those who have familiar spirits, and the wizards.
